input.content: --- name: document-editor description: Use when building, reimplementing, or fixing a Powerhouse document editor or drive app — the React UI that displays and edits documents of a given model in Connect. --- # Document Editor Document editors are scaffolded by codegen, never hand-written from scratch. Trigger the scaffold either by running `npx ph-cli generate editor --name "" --document-type ""` directly (the simpler, default route), or by registering a `powerhouse/document-editor` document in the Vetra Drive and confirming it (`ADD_DOCUMENT_TYPE` / `SET_EDITOR_NAME` / `SET_EDITOR_STATUS: CONFIRMED`) if you specifically need it tracked as a spec document. Either way, codegen produces `editors//module.ts` (generated, off-limits) and `editors//editor.tsx` (yours — the only file in the scaffold meant for hand-editing). The rule for what's off-limits anywhere in the project: a file carrying the `WARNING: DO NOT EDIT` / `This file is auto-generated and updated by codegen` JSDoc banner is regenerated and must not be touched, whether or not it lives under a folder literally named `gen/` — but the converse doesn't hold (see `editor-patterns.md`): `src/reducers/*.ts` carries no banner yet is still codegen-owned. ## Workflow 1. [Check prerequisites](references/00-check-prerequisites.md) — ED.00: confirm the reactor is running (per the `reactor-project` skill), familiarize with the document model, and scaffold the editor. 2. [Write the editor implementation](references/01-editor-implementation.md) — ED.01: clean up boilerplate, seed test documents, implement viewing then editing, resolve type/lint/format/test issues, and verify visually with Playwright. See [editor-patterns.md](references/editor-patterns.md) for the generated-hooks pattern, styling, component modularity, design-system pointers, and the two-step process for changing the underlying document model. ## Common mistakes - **Hand-writing editor files instead of scaffolding first.** `editors/editors.ts` and `editors/index.ts` are codegen-owned (DO-NOT-EDIT banner) — a document type not yet scaffolded gets its editor via `ph-cli generate editor` or Vetra Drive registration, never by creating `editors//` by hand. - **Trusting `powerhouse.config.json` / `.mcp.json` for the reactor's port.** Both can point at a different, still-live reactor. Trust only the endpoint observed in the running process's own output. - **Running a bare `switchboard` command.** It acts on its configured profile, which may default to a remote/cloud reactor. Always pass an explicit `--profile` bound to the local instance; if none exists, stop and hand the user the exact profile stanza rather than editing `~/.switchboard/profiles.toml` yourself — unless running unattended, per `reactor-project`'s [RPPM.01.2 unattended path](../reactor-project/references/01-run-and-capture-endpoint.md#rppm012-parse-and-verify-the-vetra-endpoints). - **Assuming a "missing" model is broken.** A document model with complete, passing tests can still be absent from the running supergraph until the reactor is restarted. - **Guessing Switchboard GraphQL shapes.** `findDocuments` needs `search: { type }` and returns `items`; a document's UUID and its Connect URL slug are different strings; mutations need explicit field selection. - **Checking types with `pnpm build` or `pnpm tsc`.** Use `npx tsc --noEmit` instead. `pnpm lint:fix` runs oxlint, not ESLint; run `pnpm format` (oxfmt) too if formatting still complains. - **Skipping the reducer half of a model fix.** Updating the schema via the reactor without also updating `src/reducers/` by hand leaves the bug in place after the next codegen pass. --- # Reference: 00-check-prerequisites.md # ED.00 Check the prerequisites for creating a document editor Work in the current working directory — the active Reactor Package project. Start and manage the reactor yourself per the `reactor-project` skill: run `ph vetra` as a backgrounded shell and read its accumulated output directly to see when codegen has run and what actually got bound. There is no separate supervisor process managing these for you here — invoking `ph vetra` / `ph-cli generate` yourself is the mechanism, not something to avoid. Trust only the endpoint you actually observed in that output. `powerhouse.config.json` and `.mcp.json` can point at a completely different, unrelated, but still-live reactor — never take their port numbers as fact. Read the `AGENTS.md` in the project directory for best practices. Code is regenerated automatically by Vetra's watcher once the reactor is running. - Review bugs and errors in the GraphQL types if the code generator is stuck. - Review and update the document model specification (via `switchboard docs mutate`, per the `document-modeling` skill) to fix type errors in generated code. - Consider restarting the reactor (per the `reactor-project` skill) if needed. ## ED.00.1 Familiarize yourself with the document model - Read the document model's specification (via the Switchboard GraphQL endpoint or the `switchboard` CLI, per the `document-modeling` skill) for context. - Under `document-models//`, confirm the generated types and reducers exist, and read them to understand the model's operations. - Run `pnpm test` (vitest) to verify all tests are passing. - Run `npx tsc --noEmit` to detect type errors — not `pnpm build` (invokes `ph-cli build`, far more than a typecheck) and not `pnpm tsc` (maps to bare `tsc`, which emits files instead of just checking). - **If the model doesn't show up when queried through Switchboard despite complete, tested code on disk**, don't assume it's broken: an on-disk model can be absent from the running supergraph until the reactor is restarted. Restart per the `reactor-project` skill and re-check before debugging further. Fix any issues you detect. ## ED.00.2 Scaffold the editor via the CLI (primary route) Check first whether an editor already exists for this document type: `editors/editors.ts` carries the `WARNING: DO NOT EDIT` / `This file is auto-generated and updated by codegen` JSDoc banner and lists every registered editor module. If your document type is already there, skip ahead to ED.00.4 and continue in the existing `editor.tsx`. Otherwise, scaffold a new one directly: ```bash npx ph-cli generate editor --name "" --document-type "" ``` Supply both flags explicitly even though `--help` marks them optional — take the document type verbatim from the model's exported `gen/document-type.ts` constant. The command prints nothing on success. Confirm it worked by checking the concrete artifacts, not `git status`: on a genuinely fresh `ph init` project (the state `ph init` actually leaves you in — no initial commit made yet) everything shows as untracked `??` regardless of whether it's new or pre-existing, so `git status --short` cannot distinguish "just created by this command" from "was already there." Instead confirm directly — `editors//` now exists with `editor.tsx` and `module.ts` inside it, and `powerhouse.manifest.json` contains a new `editors` entry for it (e.g. `grep -A3 '""' powerhouse.manifest.json`, or just read the file). If the project already has at least one commit, `git status --short` showing `editors/editors.ts` and `editors/index.ts` modified alongside the new untracked directory is a fine secondary check — just don't rely on it as the only signal on an uncommitted project. Run `npx ph-cli generate editor --help` if these flags ever drift. This CLI route is simpler and should be your default. ## ED.00.3 Alternative: register through the Vetra Drive Only if you specifically need the editor tracked as a document in the Vetra Drive (e.g. for a stakeholder-visible spec) rather than scaffolded directly: - Create a `powerhouse/document-editor` document on the Vetra Drive — never set its document ID manually, it's auto-assigned. - Use `ADD_DOCUMENT_TYPE` to add the target document type, `SET_EDITOR_NAME` to name the editor, then `SET_EDITOR_STATUS` set to `CONFIRMED` to trigger codegen. This is a dependent chain (each mutation needs the prior one applied first) — issue these as sequential `switchboard docs mutate` calls (camelCase `--op` names, e.g. `addDocumentType`, distinct from the SCREAMING_SNAKE action names above), never a single `switchboard docs apply`, which reverses operation order. - Wait for the same `editors//` scaffold to appear, exactly as in ED.00.2. Prefer ED.00.2 unless this specification document is genuinely needed. ## ED.00.4 Verify the code generation was triggered and boilerplate code was created - Confirm the scaffold exists at `editors//`, whichever route produced it. - `editor.tsx` has **no** DO-NOT-EDIT banner — it's pre-filled with a `DocumentToolbar`, a header info grid, and a raw `` dump, and is the file you're meant to customize. - `module.ts` alongside it **does** carry the banner (it wires `EditorModule` config and lazy-loads `editor.js`) and must not be touched. - The banner is the general rule for the whole scaffold — see `editor-patterns.md` for how it extends to `gen/` and the generated hooks file. --- # Reference: 01-editor-implementation.md # ED.01 Write the editor implementation Work in the current working directory — the active Reactor Package project. Start and manage the reactor yourself per the `reactor-project` skill: run `ph vetra` as a backgrounded shell and read its accumulated output directly to confirm codegen ran. There is no separate supervisor process managing these for you here — invoking `ph vetra` / `ph-cli generate` yourself is the mechanism, not something to avoid. See [editor-patterns.md](editor-patterns.md) for the generated-hooks pattern, styling and component-modularity guidance, and the generated-files rule — this scenario assumes you've read it. ## ED.01.1 Verify code generation and clean up the boilerplate code - Confirm the editor exists at `editors//` (see [00-check-prerequisites.md](00-check-prerequisites.md) if not). - Check whether the scaffold boilerplate is still present in `editor.tsx` (recognizable by ``) and remove it — keep the imports as hints, and keep ``. If it's already gone, it may have been cleaned up in a previous pass. - Verify `` is present; add it if not. It's imported from `@powerhousedao/design-system/connect` and gives the user document export, operation history, and the Switchboard API endpoint for this document. - Run `pnpm test` (vitest) — confirm no issues. - Run `npx tsc --noEmit` — confirm no issues. ## ED.01.2 Ensure test documents exist for verification Check the Preview Drive for existing test documents of your document type; create more if there are few or none. Never set a document ID manually when creating one. Consider a small, a medium, and a large example document; if the model has a multi-stage workflow, create documents at different stages of it. Seed data with MCP's `createDocument`/`addActions` if available, or through the Switchboard GraphQL endpoint (captured per the `reactor-project` skill) directly, or the `switchboard` CLI with an explicit `--profile` bound to your local reactor. **Never issue a bare `switchboard` command** — it acts on its configured profile, which can default to a remote/cloud reactor; if no local profile exists yet, stop and give the user the exact `[profiles.]` stanza to add (per the `reactor-project` skill) rather than editing `~/.switchboard/profiles.toml` yourself or attempting `switchboard init` non-interactively — unless running unattended with no human available to confirm, in which case follow the `reactor-project` skill's [RPPM.01.2 unattended-path exception](../../reactor-project/references/01-run-and-capture-endpoint.md#rppm012-parse-and-verify-the-vetra-endpoints) instead, and report exactly what you wrote. The Switchboard GraphQL shapes are undocumented and easy to get wrong the first time: - `findDocuments` takes `search: { type: "" }` — not a bare `documentType:` argument — and its result exposes documents under `items`, not `edges`/`results`. - The document's real UUID (from `findDocuments`) is not the URL slug Connect shows (`-`) — visually similar since the slug ends in the UUID. Mutations need the bare UUID as `docId`; the full slug fails with "Document not found." - Model mutations require an explicit field selection on the result — no selection, or a made-up field like `revision`, both fail; introspect the return type or just select `{ id }`. - Check the actual response JSON, not just exit status — a call can look like it succeeded in a combined shell command while its own response is an error. - Reading a document's own state is nested under the model's query type, not a flat field: roughly ` { document(identifier: "") { document { state { global { ... } } } } }` (the outer `` matches the model's PascalCase name, e.g. `PizzaOrderDesk`). Guessing a flatter shape (`(id: ...) { state }`, or `document(identifier: ...) { state }` with no model wrapper) fails; introspect `Queries`/`_DocumentWithChildren` via `__type(name: ...)` if the exact nesting isn't obvious. ## ED.01.3 Implement viewing functionality Focus on the reading experience first. Review any existing editor code and confirm all the document state can be comfortably explored; if something's inaccessible, decide how to expose it. **Choose the layout paradigm** based on the document model's structure: a. If the document type has a standard presentation (calendar-, kanban-, chat-, spreadsheet-like, board games, ...), use it. b. Otherwise, for content meant to be read/produced sequentially (text documents, forms, invoices, specs — good PDF/print candidates), use a single scrolling document-flow view, Notion-style. c. For data meant to be searched, browsed, and updated more than read start-to-finish (collections, catalogues), use an app paradigm: full-height layout, tabs/menus, more structured navigation. d. Mix (b) and (c) when most of the document is flow-like but some sections (settings, option lists) are more functional. Unless told otherwise, use a sober SaaS-style design: white background, rounded corners, grey accents/borders, soft shadows, color reserved for labels/chips/warnings. **Structure the navigation:** - A sidebar for root-level scalars/scalar-arrays/simple-object children, if there's enough of them to warrant one; otherwise a header. - Tables in the main area for root-level object collections — all properties as columns if there are few; selectable rows with full detail in a sidebar if there are many. - For nested collections, an inbox-style UI: top-level item summaries in a sidebar, full detail plus nested collections in the main area once selected. - `` tags (with size constraints) for URL fields that reference images. - Tabs sparingly. Build one component at a time, keep `` alone at the top, and bring the pieces together into the chosen layout. ## ED.01.4 Implement editing functionality Make every reachable part of the state editable via `dispatch`, following the hooks/dispatch pattern in [editor-patterns.md](editor-patterns.md): - Buttons/icons/toggles/checkboxes for parameterless actions (remove, binary status flips, reordering). - A single input with dispatch-on-blur for single-parameter actions (simple setters, single-field object creation). - An inline form where a few properties are needed and there's room for it. - A sidebar pane or a modal (semi-transparent overlay) for larger objects or multi-step input. - A pop-up with a URL field and preview for editable images. - Prefer hover-to-reveal inline editing over "edit mode" buttons. - Keep `` alone at the top. Checklist: every reachable state is directly or indirectly editable; collections support add/remove where the operations allow it; every `dispatch` call is strongly typed with the right parameters. ## ED.01.5 Resolve outstanding issues - Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and fix anything it reports. **Never** use `any` or type casts in reducers or in dispatch calls — both are the load-bearing typed surface of the editor. - Run `pnpm lint:fix` — this runs **oxlint** (`oxlint --type-aware --type-check --fix`), not ESLint. Resolve whatever it can't auto-fix. - Run `pnpm format:check` (oxfmt); if it fails, run `pnpm format` to auto-fix, then re-check. A clean lint pass doesn't guarantee clean formatting. - **`pnpm format` reformats the whole project, not just your changes** — it can rewrite files you never touched, including other document models you were told to leave alone. After running it, check `git status`/`git diff` and revert (`git checkout -- `) anything outside the files you actually meant to change. Prefer running `oxfmt` directly on just your changed paths (e.g. `npx oxfmt editors//`) over the whole-project `pnpm format` when you can. - Run `pnpm test` (vitest) — confirm it's still passing. ## ED.01.6 Visual verification with Playwright Use the `playwright-cli` skill to visually verify the editor in a real browser. Open the Vetra Studio URL, navigate to a test document in the Preview Drive, and verify: - The editor loads without console errors. - Document state displays correctly. - Editing interactions (add, edit, delete) work as expected. - `` is visible at the top. **If the `playwright-cli` binary isn't installed** (e.g. `npx --no-install playwright-cli --version` fails with "could not determine executable to run", and no global install exists either), fall back to any `mcp__*playwright*` browser-automation MCP tools available in the session — navigate, snapshot, click, and read console messages with those instead; the same four checks above still apply. **If no browser automation is available at all** (neither the CLI nor an MCP fallback), degrade to static verification instead of skipping this step: re-run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `pnpm test`, read the final `editor.tsx` and its components once more against the ED.01.3/ED.01.4 checklists, and say explicitly in your report that visual verification was not possible in this environment. Fix any issues found and re-verify. Take a screenshot of the final result when a browser is available. --- # Reference: editor-patterns.md # Editor Implementation Patterns ## Required imports and setup Every single-document-type editor follows the same shape. Using a `Todo` document model as an illustrative example: ```typescript import { generateId } from "document-model/core"; import { actions, useSelectedTodoDocument } from "document-models/todo"; export default function Editor() { const [document, dispatch] = useSelectedTodoDocument(); function handleAddTodo(values: { title: string }) { if (values.title) { dispatch(actions.addTodo({ id: generateId(), title: values.title })); } } // ... } ``` There is **no `editors/hooks/` directory** — the hook is not co-located with the editor at all. `useSelectedTodoDocument` (or `useSelectedDocument` for your model) is **generated** and lives in the model's own package, at `document-models//v1/hooks.ts`, re-exported from the model package root (`document-models/`) alongside `actions`. It wraps the generic `useSelectedDocument()` from `@powerhousedao/reactor-browser`, asserts the document type, and returns `[document, dispatch]`. You never write it yourself; if it's missing, the scaffold hasn't been generated yet (see `00-check-prerequisites.md`). The action creators you dispatch (`actions.addTodo`, off the single `actions` object re-exporting every module's creators) are generated too — read the model's actual `creators.ts` to see the exact input shape an action needs rather than guessing field names. ## Styling Use Tailwind classes, or a scoped `
